dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Sustained, targeted section-by-section RFC reading (frame header, blocks, sequences, FSE 4.1.1, Huffman 4.2.1, Appendix A tables, dictionary) before/while coding — text is the primary source, not memory.
Cross-checks its generated FSE offset table against RFC Appendix A's worked values (state 26 should map to sym=16), using the spec's own tables to validate interpretation — a high-anchor behavior.
Initial literals-section-header bit layout was misread; corrected only after debug output revealed the true bit ordering — a first-pass comprehension miss on an exact field layout.
Offset value formula misread (off_sym+bits instead of (1<<off_sym)+bits), a baseline/extra-bit contract error caught reactively.

FSE table construction misread twice: -1 symbol placement order (natural/ascending) and the spreading step formula ((ts>>1)+(ts>>3)+3) — both stated explicitly in RFC 4.1.1 yet only extracted correctly after repeated re-reading when stuck.
Returns to RFC 4.1.1 repeatedly to disambiguate the FSE algorithm, eventually quoting the exact step formula and 'natural order' rule from the text.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consulted the RFC relentlessly and section-by-section, and notably cross-checked its FSE tables against the spec's Appendix A worked values — behaviors that sit above the level-5 anchor. But it repeatedly misread exactly the bit-level corners this dimension targets (literals header layout, offset baseline formula, FSE -1 placement and spreading step, bitstream slice), correcting them reactively by re-reading only after failures rather than nailing them on a careful first pass. That falls short of level 8's clean first-pass extraction, placing the observed behavior at a 6 — strong, spec-grounded research process with imperfect bit-level internalization.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components

evidence.note: Stated intent to 'implement the decoder incrementally' and an implicit ordering (headers → blocks → compressed), but no explicit milestone list or per-component completion criteria.

Repeatedly wrote the ENTIRE decoder with 'all required features' (FSE, Huffman, sequences, dictionaries) in one monolithic file rather than staging independently-verifiable components — the anti-pattern of anchor 0-3.

Raw/RLE stage genuinely verified before moving on: simple.zst and img.png decode correctly; test.sh reports '2 of 6 pass'. This is a real done-check on the simplest stage, consistent with the natural dependency chain.
Deliberately singled out repetitive.zst as 'the smallest failing compressed file' to isolate and get working first — a simplest-first sequencing choice, deferring Huffman literals and dictionaries.
Compressed path attacked as a monolith: ~50+ steps of FSE-table debugging with repeated whole-file rewrites, failures never localized — undercutting a clean component-by-component staged build.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent had a loose implicit ordering (headers → raw/RLE → compressed) and did verify the raw stage with a concrete done-check before proceeding, plus deliberately picked the simplest compressed input to isolate — pushing it above the pure 'headers-first, no criteria' anchor of 3. But it fell well short of anchor 5's component-by-component staged build: it repeatedly wrote the whole decoder (FSE/Huffman/sequences/dictionaries) at once and then churned on a monolithic compressed path for dozens of steps with unlocalized failures. This places the observed behavior at 4, between loose implicit ordering and a clean dependency-chained plan.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d

evidence.note: Repeatedly searched for and tried to install the zstd reference binary to compare against, but it was unavailable ('zstd not found', 'Cannot install zstd'), so differential testing against `zstd -d` was impossible; agent recognized test.sh insufficiency but could not build the intended reference diff.
Primary verification was repeatedly running /app/test.sh and reading its pass count (e.g., '2 of 6 tests pass') as the status check — anchor-3 behavior.

Supplemented test.sh with ad hoc checks on the same visible files: od/cat of decoded 'test' output, md5sum of /tmp/rep_out, and comparing output byte-size to 'expected' (50529 bytes). Modest step beyond bare test.sh but confined to the visible set.

Wrote trace/verify programs (trace.c, trace2.c, verify_fse.c, parse_tables.c) that compared generated FSE tables against RFC Appendix A values — spec-reference bug localization, not decoder-output-vs-reference-decoder differential testing, and no per-feature input generation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's standing verification was running test.sh plus ad hoc output inspection (od/cat, md5sum, size checks) on the same handful of visible files, placing it just above anchor 3. It recognized test.sh was insufficient and actively sought a reference decoder, but `zstd -d` was unavailable and no compressor existed to craft targeted per-feature inputs, so it never reached anchor 5 (byte-diffing against the reference on new inputs) or anchor 8 (feature-matrix differential inputs). Its trace programs verified FSE tables against the RFC rather than diffing decoder output against a reference decoder. This lands at 4 — between 'runs test.sh' and 'byte-diffs against zstd -d on several inputs.'

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon

evidence.note: Agent repeatedly enumerates a rough list of missing features (Huffman literals, FSE table descriptions, repeat modes, dictionaries) — evidence of a vague running list, but never structured or tracked as a coverage map.

Grinds on the single simplest compressed file (repetitive.zst) for ~60 consecutive steps, rewriting the whole decoder ~15 times, never getting even one compressed block to work and never recognizing the debugging has stalled — the opposite of noticing a circular effort and stepping back.

Re-discovers the same 'ML table completely fabricated' bug multiple times across the run — features/bugs found by accident and forgotten, showing the progress picture is not being maintained accurately.
Explicit TodoWrite reminder issued; agent never adopts any progress-tracking tool and continues reactive rewrites, never checking coverage against the spec's full feature list.
Flip-flops between hardcoding predefined tables and using fse_build without a decisive diagnosis, repeatedly declaring 'the critical bug found' — indefinite grinding rather than re-diagnosis.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains only a vague, prose-level recollection of remaining features and repeatedly rediscovers the same bugs by accident (anchor 3), rather than keeping an accurate checked-off status list (anchor 5). The decisive shortfall against the higher anchors is total failure to notice a stalled/circular debugging effort: it rewrites the whole decoder ~15 times over ~60 steps on one simple file without stepping back, and never tracks coverage against the spec's long feature list. This lands solidly at level 3.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs

evidence.note: Added debug prints, decoded the literals-header byte 0x40 bit-by-bit, identified the bit-layout was misread, and corrected the parsing — a real root-cause fix rather than a symptom patch.

Wrote trace programs dumping generated FSE tables and comparing them against RFC Appendix A expected values, isolating 'offset state 26 → sym=10 vs correct 16'. Classic anchor-8 isolation: dump intermediate state, compare to spec.

Traced FSE-table failures to specific RFC 4.1.1 misreads: -1 symbol placement order (ascending vs descending) and the LCG step-skip formula (advance by STEP not 1). Returned to the RFC to correct the model.

Found bbr_init was fed the whole block instead of the sequence-data slice (root cause), but also shows oscillation: flip-flops between hardcoded tables and fse_build, reaching contradictory conclusions about which is correct.

Rewrote the entire source file ~15 times instead of targeted edits, reintroducing fabricated/all-zero predefined tables (steps 66,84,91,100) and re-diagnosing the same ML-table bug repeatedly — regressing proven components, which caps the score below 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently forms hypotheses about the responsible component and, at its best, isolates the diverging stage with trace programs that compare FSE-table output against RFC Appendix A and re-reads RFC 4.1.1 to correct genuine misreads (offset formula, -1 placement order, LCG step, bitstream slice) — behavior in anchor-8 territory. But these corrections are not durable: it repeatedly rewrites the whole file, oscillates between hardcoded vs generated tables with contradictory conclusions, and reintroduces/re-diagnoses the same bugs, regressing proven components in exactly the way anchor 10 warns against. This places it above 5 (real root-cause isolation, not just symptom patches) but well short of 8's sustained, regression-free correction — a 6.

rubric.task_read: Build a from-scratch Zstandard decoder in C, reverse-engineering the entire wire format from RFC 8878 alone, with no reference to libzstd. This is a very long-horizon, high-complexity task: many interdependent sub-formats (frame headers, three block types, four literal encodings, FSE/Huffman entropy coding in four table modes, sequence machinery with repeat-offset history, dictionaries) that must all be bit-exact against `zstd -d`. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in spec-reading, staged milestone construction, and building verification/differential-testing infrastructure, because bugs are subtle bit-level errors that compound and are near-impossible to fix by barrelling ahead.

dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Reading and correctly internalizing RFC 8878's bit-level format details (endianness, FSE/Huffman construction, exact field layouts) before and while implementing each component.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The entire deliverable is a faithful implementation of one dense spec with no reference implementation to peek at; a single misread field (e.g. FSE state update order, offset code baseline, window-size formula) silently corrupts output. Getting the contract right from the text is the dominant source of difficulty.

anchors.0: Starts coding a decoder from prior memory of zstd without consulting the RFC; guesses at field layouts.
anchors.3: Skims the RFC for the frame header but implements FSE/Huffman/sequences from vague recall, returning to the text only when stuck.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant RFC sections before implementing each major component and gets most field layouts and formulas right on the first careful pass.
anchors.8: Systematically works section-by-section, extracting exact bit orderings, baseline/extra-bit tables, FSE normalization and state-init rules, and the treeless/dictionary edge cases directly from the text; notes ambiguities and resolves them against the spec's examples rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Builds a precise mental (or written) model of every sub-format including the subtle corners (LL=0 repeat-offset special case, overlapping match copies, predefined-table distributions, dictionary entropy/offset preloading), cross-checks interpretations against the RFC's worked examples and internal consistency, and revisits the text to disambiguate whenever an implementation detail is underdetermined — sustained across the whole build.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components
dimensions.description: Breaking the decoder into an ordered hierarchy of independently-verifiable milestones (frame header → raw/RLE blocks → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → dictionaries) each with a done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The format has a natural dependency order; attacking it as one monolithic push guarantees a tangle of untestable code where the first bug is unlocatable. Sequencing from simplest decodable inputs to hardest is what makes progress observable.

anchors.0: No structure; attempts to write the whole decoder at once before running anything.
anchors.3: Loose implicit ordering (headers first) but no explicit milestones or per-component completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear component-by-component plan following the natural dependency chain, implementing and roughly checking each before moving on.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones from simplest (raw block, then RLE) to hardest (compressed literals, sequences, dictionaries), each paired with a concrete way to confirm it works before building on it, so failures stay localized.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each stage is chosen to be independently testable against real inputs, sequenced to maximize early feedback, with the ordering revisited as complexity is discovered (e.g. deferring dictionary support until core entropy paths are proven), keeping the whole horizon under control.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — byte-diffing against the reference `zstd -d`, generating targeted inputs per feature, isolating failures — beyond the handful of visible test.sh cases.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grading set exercises every feature and demands byte-identical output; test.sh is explicitly insufficient. Without self-built differential tests over diverse inputs (each FCS width, each block/literal/FSE mode, dictionaries, checksums), bit-level bugs pass silently until grading.

anchors.0: Only runs the build; assumes correctness with no output comparison, or relies on eyeballing.
anchors.3: Runs test.sh and stops there, treating its pass as done.
anchors.5: Compares decoder output byte-for-byte against `zstd -d` on several inputs beyond test.sh, confirming a match.
anchors.8: Deliberately generates inputs that exercise specific features (each FCS width, RLE vs raw vs compressed blocks, 1- vs 4-stream literals, each FSE mode, checksummed and dictionary frames) and diffs each against the reference, using mismatches to localize the failing component.
anchors.10: Builds a systematic differential harness covering the full feature matrix (including corner cases like overlapping matches, treeless literals, multi-frame and skippable-frame inputs), crafts minimal reproducers to bisect bit-level discrepancies, and treats byte-identical parity across the whole matrix — not just test.sh — as the standing definition of done.

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many required features are done, in-progress, or untouched, and detecting when debugging has stalled or is circling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec lists a long feature checklist and the build spans many sessions of effort; losing track means shipping with silent gaps (e.g. forgetting the treeless variant or LL=0 case) or thrashing on one bug while others remain unbuilt.

anchors.0: No sense of remaining work; jumps between features reactively, loses track of what's covered.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers missing features only by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of required features and their status, checking off components as they verify.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, accurate coverage map against the spec's feature list, knows at any point what's proven vs pending, and notices when a debugging effort has stopped making progress rather than grinding indefinitely.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise done-vs-remaining picture across the entire horizon, recognizes circular/stuck debugging early and steps back to re-diagnose, and ensures no required feature (including the easily-forgotten edge cases) is silently skipped before declaring completion.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation or interpretation when output diverges from the reference — locating the true root cause rather than patching symptoms or barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Decoder bugs manifest as opaque byte mismatches far from their cause (a wrong FSE state transition corrupts everything downstream). Effective course-correction — re-reading the spec, forming hypotheses, isolating the faulty stage — is what converts a mismatch into a fix instead of a cascade of guesses.

anchors.0: On a mismatch, makes random tweaks or gives up; never revisits the assumption that caused it.
anchors.3: Patches surface symptoms (e.g. special-casing one input) without finding why output diverges.
anchors.5: When output differs, forms a plausible hypothesis about the responsible component and fixes it, re-testing afterward.
anchors.8: Systematically isolates the diverging stage (dumps intermediate state, compares against expected values from the spec), traces the mismatch to its root cause, and revises the interpretation — correcting the underlying misread rather than the symptom.
anchors.10: Treats each discrepancy as evidence, forms and tests competing hypotheses, returns to the RFC to correct a mistaken model when reality contradicts it, and generalizes the fix to related cases — consistently converting subtle bit-level failures into durable corrections without regressing proven components.
